data.title: Suspicious letter: "new bank details" from Stadtwerke
data.summary: A letter dated 7 September 2026, claiming to be from Stadtwerke Musterstadt, says its bank details have changed. It demands €214.00 by 11 September 2026 to a new IBAN and threatens to cut off power. It shows several signs of a scam.
data.explanation: This letter looks like a payment-redirect scam. Real utilities rarely change bank details this way, and they don't threaten a shutdown "without further notice" or tell you not to reply. The account holder is a different company (Global Energy Payments s.r.o.), and the contact is a mobile number. Don't pay and don't call the number in the letter. Check with Stadtwerke using contact details from your last genuine bill or their official website. Look at your contract or previous invoices to confirm your real Abschlag and account. You could also report it to the consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police.

warnings: Likely scam: the letter announces a new bank account held by an unrelated company (Global Energy Payments s.r.o.), not by the Stadtwerke.
It threatens a power cut without further notice and sets a very short payment deadline.
It tells you not to reply and to call only a special mobile number, which is a common fraud pattern.
The sender's email domain (kundenservice-mail.example) doesn't look like an official Stadtwerke address.
The letter says direct debits can't be collected, so check your bank statements and your real account with Stadtwerke.
